me-ld-307-hp-207-132nd-legislature.sponsors: Rep. Melanie Sachs; original bill page also identifies Rep. Drew Gattine on adopted amendment H-1051
me-ld-307-hp-207-132nd-legislature.status: Passed both chambers (House enactment vote 83-66, 2026-04-08); vetoed by Gov. Janet Mills 2026-04-24; House override attempt failed 72-65 (92 needed for 2/3) on 2026-04-29; Veto Sustained, 2026-04-29
me-ld-307-hp-207-132nd-legislature.key_provisions: Would have prohibited any municipality, state agency, or quasi-independent state entity from accepting applications or issuing permits, certificates, or approvals for development, construction, or operation of a data center with a load of 20 MW or more until 2027-11-01. Would have created the Maine Data Center Coordination Council to study ratepayer, grid reliability, environmental, host-community, data-sharing, impact fee, demand response, and community benefit agreement issues, with report due 2027-02-01.

me-ld-713-hp-452-132nd-legislature-publi.bill: LD 713 / HP 452, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2026, c. 768
me-ld-713-hp-452-132nd-legislature-publi.status: Signed by Governor 2026-04-23; official chapter citation Public Law 2025, c. 768 (132nd Legislature, enacted in 2026).
me-ld-713-hp-452-132nd-legislature-publi.key_provisions: Public Law 2025, chapter 768 excludes property in data centers beginning operations on or after August 1, 2026 from the business equipment exemption; excludes data-center services from the Dirigo eligible-sector definition and separately excludes data-center businesses beginning operations on or after that date; directs an incentives study and report due November 4, 2026.

me-ld-912-sp-402-132nd-legislature-publi.bill: LD 912 / SP 402, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2025, c. 85
me-ld-912-sp-402-132nd-legislature-publi.status: Emergency enacted and signed by Governor 2025-05-23, Public Law 2025 c. 85
me-ld-912-sp-402-132nd-legislature-publi.key_provisions: Amended Title 35-A definition of transmission and distribution utility. A private-distribution exception for a northern Maine commercial or industrial site does not apply if more than 25% of the entity's nameplate capacity serves data centers on that site.
